newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close down on regional weakness.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close down on regional weakness.

text.p: Jakarta share prices closed lower on Monday following bearish sentiment almost across the board due to weak regional markets, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 2.59 points, or 0.47 percent, to 545.02 points. Losers led gainers by 74 to 26, with 41 counters unchanged.

"Overall market sentiment was bearish, many brokers continued to offload shares following a drop in the Dow on Friday. Also, weakness in regional markets today dampened sentiment in Jakarta," said one foreign broker.
Brokers said the continued selling also stemmed from market concern about the decline in foreign investment in Indonesia.

"Foreigners are cautious over the decline, whether it's due to purely sentiment or fundamental aspects such as a hike in workers' wages in Indonesia or risk," said one analyst from a foreign brokerage.

Indonesian Investment Minister Sanyoto Sastrowardoyo said on Monday foreign investment approvals from January 1 to August 31 this year totalled $22.2 billion against $29.7 billion in the year-ago period.
Property and hotel firm Mas Murni Indonesia topped the active list with 15.6 million shares traded, rising 25 rupiah to 825.
Brokers said the rise was due to market talk of a possible take-over by a Singaporean firm and a rights issue.
Conglomerate Bakrie Brothers gained 175 rupiah to 2,250 on a volume of 1.9 million shares following positive sentiment generated by first-half results announced last week.

Garment firm Karwell fell 325 rupiah, or 20 percent, to 1,250 as brokers offloaded stocks after sharp rises last week. The share had risen on talk of a possible joint venture but brokers said on Monday the rumours were unfounded.
